value: Whole-brain results showed a significant main effect of stimulus (CS+ > CS−) in the fusiformis gyrus, posterior cingulate cortex, supplementary motor area, middle frontal gyrus, and cerebellum. ROI analyses found significant effects in the bilateral ventral striatum, ACC, OFC, insula, and thalamus, with a trend in the bilateral amygdala, indicating successfully conditioned hemodynamic responses.

spans.text: Whole‐brain results showed a significant main effect of stimulus (CS+ > CS−) in the fusiformis gyrus ( x / y / z = 30/−70/−11, z max = 6.73; P < 0.001), the posterior cingulate cortex ( x / y / z = −6/−28/28, z max = 6.22; P < 0.001), the supplementary motor area ( x / y / z = 6/14/46, z max = 6.18; P = 0.001), the middle frontal gyrus ( x / y / z = −30/53/28, z max = 4.85; P = 0.019), and the cerebellum ( x / y / z = −39/−55/−50, z max = 4.83; P < 0.021). Regarding ROI analyses, we found a significant main effect of stimulus in the contrast CS+ > CS− in the bilateral ventral striatum, the ACC, the OFC, the insula, the thalamus and a trend in the bilateral amygdala (see Table 1 ), thus indicating successfully conditioned hemodynamic responses .
